Listen to this article Share For some moviegoers, the conversation after watching The Perfect Spec has gone beyond finding the right person. Since the film opened in Nigerian cinemas on Friday, November 6, audiences have shared personal reflections, prayed together, and drawn parallels between its storyline and their own experiences of faith, relationships, and waiting on God. One audience member, reflecting on her experience after a screening, described the film as “cute, light, easy to watch with a lasting impression”. She said it reminded her of what faith can accomplish when people choose obedience, trust God, and let Him lead, even when they do not understand His plans. She also recalled five women seated beside her who prayed together after the screening, with three expressing their desire to receive the blessing they believed the film had affirmed. The experience echoes responses from the film’s exclusive premiere, where 11 people reportedly reconnected with their faith in Jesus. These reactions suggest that the film’s reception extends beyond its romantic comedy appeal to the personal and spiritual conversations it has inspired. Beyond the cinema: A story inspiring personal reflections Such responses offer an early indication of the engagement The Perfect Spec is generating beyond the cinema screen. During its opening weekend, cast members and the production team visited cinema locations to meet audiences. Conversations have touched on personal experiences of heartbreak and singleness, marriage, discernment, faith and the challenge of surrendering personal expectations. The film has also inspired an outpouring of support and generosity from people with no prior connection to the production. Directed by award-winning filmmaker Michelle Bello, The Perfect Spec follows Oye, a 32-year-old overachiever and self-proclaimed ‘Jesus Baby’ who, after another disappointing heartbreak, decides to give up on men. However, when unexpected romantic possibilities and an unlikely intervention disrupt her carefully laid plans, Oye is forced to confront her expectations of love, her convictions and her understanding of God’s timing. Written and produced by sibling duo Ololade Okedare and Ayobola Eniola, the film explores familiar questions about Christian dating and marriage through the accessible format of a romantic comedy. Rather than treating faith as separate from the everyday complications of relationships, it places it within relatable experiences, including attraction, uncertainty, emotional disappointments, pressure to marry and the temptation to make life happen according to one’s own timetable. Kinsman Studios’ vision: Making faith-based films relatable For Kinsman Studios, the audience response affirms its creative ambition to make faith-based films that are not defined solely by religious themes but also by their ability to entertain, connect with audiences and tell recognisably human stories. “With The Perfect Spec, we wanted to tell a story that people could genuinely enjoy and see themselves in, while also creating room for deeper reflection,” said Ololade Okedare, writer and producer. “Oye’s journey touches on something many people understand: the desire for love, the pressure of expectations and the difficulty of trusting God when life doesn’t follow the plan we’ve made for ourselves. “We’ve been so encouraged by the conversations the film is already inspiring. If people leave the cinema entertained but also thinking differently about their lives and their relationship with God, then we’ve achieved something meaningful.” Fellow writer and producer Ayobola Eniola said there was room for faith-based films to achieve commercial success without compromising the convictions that inspire them. “We believe there’s room for faith-based films to be commercially entertaining without compromising the convictions that inspire them. The Perfect Spec is a romantic comedy first and foremost, but its message is one we believe everyone can take something from. “You don’t have to share Oye’s faith to recognise the questions she faces, understand her experiences or appreciate the wisdom in the story. We want as many people as possible to experience this film,” Eniola said. Star-studded cast brings the story to life The movie stars Bamike ‘BamBam’ Olawunmi, Vine Olugu and Samuel ‘Limoblaze’ Onwubiko, alongside Segilola Ogidan, Seun Ajayi, Nonso Odogwu, Vera Ephraim, Shamz Garuba, Ifeanyi Kalu, Tolu Odewumi, Gbemi Akinlade and Fiyinfoluwa C.P. Okedare. Executive producers Ajoke Silva and Soji Jacobs are attached to the project through their production banner, Lufodo Productions. Other executive producers include Tochukwu MACFOY (drfoy) and Ewoma Luther-Abegunde. As The Perfect Spec moves beyond its opening weekend, audiences are being encouraged to see the film in cinemas nationwide and, for those who have already watched it, to bring someone else along. The conversations may begin with love and relationships, but the film’s central question reaches further: what happens when people make room for God’s wisdom instead of insisting on their own plans?
